_readme: THE SWITCH LIBRARY. Phase 6.2. Loaded by scripts/load-switches.js.
~46 facts about a company that decide which requirements apply. Layer 2 of the four in
CLAUDE.md §1: AI determines, the user can override, and NOTHING here is ever asserted as
a compliance status — that is layer 3, which is code.
THIS LIST WAS DERIVED FROM THE LIBRARY, NOT FROM THE DESIGN DOCUMENT.
CHEMICAL-OR-WA.md §2.4 proposed 46 switches. Reading all 188 trigger_condition prose
strings in requirement_templates found that 6 of them no requirement uses, and that 48
requirements depend on 30 facts §2.4 has no switch for. §2.4 was written before the
library existed and it shows. DECISIONS.md §36 records the gap and what was done.
FOUR RULES FOR ADDING A SWITCH.
1. A SWITCH EXISTS BECAUSE A REQUIREMENT'S TRIGGER NEEDS IT. Not because it seems like
a useful thing to know. Every entry below names the requirement(s) it gates in
`notes`, and an entry that names none is either seeded-but-unused (marked as such,
deliberately kept) or should not be here.
2. NO ARRAYS, NO JSONB, NO MULTI-VALUE SWITCHES. DECISIONS.md §23.1: one substance per
switch. The test is whether applies_expression would ever have to look INSIDE a
value. If it would, decompose.
3. THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH MUST NOT CYCLE, AND NO CONSTRAINT CAN ENFORCE THAT.
switches_no_self_dependency stops A -> A only; A -> B -> A is fully representable and
the foreign key is satisfied by both rows existing. The loader walks the graph and
refuses a cycle. See oil_storage_aboveground_gallons for the pair that nearly was one.
4. THRESHOLDS ARE READ FROM THE TRIGGER PROSE, NEVER ASSUMED. employee_count carries
[6,10,15,20,25,50,100] because those are the seven numbers the library actually
names. If you cannot point at the requirement the number came from, it does not go in.

switches.label: State the site is in
switches.question_plain: Which state is this site in?
switches.notes: Gates every Oregon row (94 live). Comes from geocoding the address, never from asking — DECISIONS.md §25. entity_county is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: migration 009 put the authoritative county on entities, and a switch would be a fifth free-text place to disagree (AUDIT-CHECKS.md check 9).

switches.label: What the business does with chemicals
switches.question_plain: Do you manufacture, blend, repackage, distribute, or toll process?
switches.notes: Gates HazCom manufacturer/importer duties, TSCA Inventory and CDR, TSCA adverse-reaction and substantial-risk records, TRI supplier notification.

switches.label: Employs anyone
switches.question_plain: Do you have employees other than the owner?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4 AND NEEDED BY 9 REQUIREMENTS — payroll tax, I-9, workers' comp, USERRA, safety committee, PPE assessment, OregonSaves, Oregon payroll accounts, fatality reporting. Looks trivially true and is not: Oregon's safety-committee rule exempts a sole owner who is the only employee.

switches.label: Employees, enterprise-wide
switches.question_plain: How many people do you employ in total?
switches.notes: A NUMBER, NOT BANDS, AND THE REASON IS NOT PRECISION. §2.4 proposed bands 1-10/11-19/20-24/25-49/50-99/100+. Three of the seven thresholds the library names — 6, 10 and 15 — fall INSIDE a band, so a banded value cannot answer them at all. 15 gates ADA, Title VII and the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act; a company in the 11-19 band is unresolvable against all three. Bands do not lose precision, they make three federal statutes unanswerable. companies.employee_count has been integer since migration 006. Annual because every threshold reads 'in the prior year' or '20 weeks in the current or preceding year'.

switches.label: Employees at this site
switches.question_plain: How many people work at this site?
switches.notes: SPLIT FROM employee_count because one switch cannot be both. Oregon sick time reads '10+ Oregon employees or 6+ with a Portland location' — enterprise and site in one sentence. WARN reads 'covered loss at a single site'. Rows needing site scope name THIS switch in applies_expression; everything else names employee_count.

switches.label: Has non-exempt employees
switches.question_plain: Do you have hourly or otherwise non-exempt staff?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Gates FLSA minimum wage and time records, Oregon meal and rest periods, and manufacturing daily overtime — the last of which is an Oregon distinctive (overtime after 10 hours/day in a manufacturing establishment).

switches.label: Offers a group health plan
switches.question_plain: Do you offer a group health plan?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Gates federal COBRA (20+ employees) and Oregon Mini-COBRA (fewer than 20) — two requirements that are mutually exclusive on employee_count and both conditional on this.

switches.label: Sponsors an ERISA plan
switches.question_plain: Do you sponsor a retirement or welfare benefit plan?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Gates ERISA plan documents and Form 5500, and inverts for OregonSaves — an employer with NO qualified plan must facilitate OregonSaves.

switches.label: Is a federal contractor
switches.question_plain: Do you hold federal contracts or subcontracts?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Lowers the EEO-1 Component 1 threshold from 100 employees to 50.

switches.label: Uses non-compete agreements
switches.question_plain: Do you ask any employees to sign non-compete agreements?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Oregon's restrictions are unusually specific — salary floor, exempt status, 12-month maximum, written notice — so this is a real gate rather than a formality.

switches.label: Creates employee medical or exposure records
switches.question_plain: Do you carry out medical surveillance or exposure monitoring?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Computed: true whenever any exposure_* switch is true, because every substance standard mandates monitoring or surveillance. Gates the 30-year record retention and access rule.

switches.label: Operates more than one facility
switches.question_plain: Do you operate more than one facility?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — no requirement's trigger names it today. Kept deliberately: it becomes load-bearing the moment a customer has a second site, and migration 010 already gives every company a site row so the structure is there waiting. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: Operates in more than one state
switches.question_plain: Do you operate in more than one state?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — no trigger names it. Kept: the library is Oregon-only today and the first Washington customer makes this the switch that decides which of two state plans applies. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: Owns or leases the facility
switches.question_plain: Do you own or lease this site?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — no trigger names it. §2.4 justifies it as affecting permit and tank obligations, which is plausible and not yet in the library. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: Holds an ISO certification
switches.question_plain: Do you hold ISO 9001 or ISO 14001?
switches.notes: Gates the two ISO certificate-maintenance rows. Those are contractual (jurisdiction_layer NULL, no agency) — they are obligations to a registrar, not to a regulator. Annual: certificates lapse.

switches.label: Customer-imposed compliance obligations
switches.question_plain: Do any customers or trade bodies impose audit or compliance requirements on you?
switches.notes: Gates NACD Responsible Distribution verification, the third contractual row.

switches.label: Imports or exports
switches.question_plain: Do you import or export chemicals?
switches.notes: Gates TSCA import certification, TSCA §12(b) export notification, and BIS export controls and AES filing.

switches.label: Hazardous chemicals in the workplace
switches.question_plain: Are employees exposed to hazardous chemicals in normal use or a foreseeable emergency?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4 and it is the root of the chemical branch. Produced by the Workplace Hazard Communication determination. Nearly everything below gates on it being true.

switches.label: Corrosive materials that could contact eyes or body
switches.question_plain: Could anyone's eyes or body contact an injurious corrosive material?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Gates emergency eyewash and shower suitability, and the first-aid and medical-services row.

switches.label: Listed substance above PSM/RMP threshold
switches.question_plain: Does any process hold a listed substance above its threshold quantity, or 10,000 lb of a covered flammable?
switches.notes: Gates OSHA Process Safety Management, the EPA Risk Management Program, the RMP 2024 SCCAP amendments, and the CFATS legal-status watch. NOT NUMERIC: the threshold is per substance from Appendix A, not one number, so a single quantity cannot express it. Decomposing per substance would be unbounded — this is the open case §23.1's reversal condition anticipates.

switches.label: Extremely hazardous substance above TPQ
switches.question_plain: Do you hold any EPCRA extremely hazardous substance above its threshold planning quantity?
switches.notes: Gates EPCRA §302 emergency-planning notification, §304 release notification, and the CERCLA reportable-quantity notice. Per-substance TPQ, so not numeric — same reason as psm_rmp_threshold.

switches.label: Chemical above the EPCRA Tier II threshold
switches.question_plain: Did any hazardous chemical exceed 10,000 lb — or an EHS exceed 500 lb or its TPQ — at any time last year?
switches.notes: Gates EPCRA §311 SDS submission and §312 Tier II inventory. NOT NUMERIC, and this is the one I would most like to be: the threshold is PER CHEMICAL (10,000 lb, or the lower of 500 lb and the TPQ for an EHS), so a single site-level quantity cannot express it and one switch per chemical is unbounded. An open modelling question for 6.3, not a decision taken here.

switches.label: Above an Oregon Community Right to Know threshold
switches.question_plain: Do you hold a hazardous substance above Oregon's reporting quantity — commonly 5 gallons liquid, 10 lb solid, or 20 cubic feet gas?
switches.notes: OREGON ONLY, AND LOWER THAN FEDERAL. A facility below the federal Tier II threshold can still owe an Oregon CR2K survey, so 'not required to file Tier II' does not answer this. jurisdiction_variant = true. Not numeric: three different units (gallons, pounds, cubic feet) in one rule.

switches.label: TRI-listed chemical above an activity threshold
switches.question_plain: Do you manufacture, process, or otherwise use a TRI-listed chemical above its threshold?
switches.notes: Gates the TRI Form R/A report, TRI supplier notification, and Oregon's Toxics Use and Hazardous Waste Reduction plan. Thresholds are 25,000 lb manufactured or processed and 10,000 lb otherwise used, with much lower PBT and PFAS thresholds — per chemical, so not numeric.

switches.label: Handles a TSCA risk-managed substance
switches.question_plain: Do you handle methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, or another substance under a TSCA risk-management rule?
switches.notes: Gates the three TSCA risk-management rules, SNUR screening, and the TSCA Inventory/PMN row. Annual: EPA adds substances.

switches.label: Manufactured or imported PFAS 2011-2022
switches.question_plain: Did you manufacture or import PFAS, or articles containing PFAS, at any time between 2011 and 2022?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Genuinely static — it asks about a closed historical window, which is unusual here and worth noting: nothing a company does now can change the answer.

switches.label: Non-acute hazardous waste generated per month
switches.question_plain: Roughly how many kilograms of hazardous waste do you generate in a typical month?
switches.notes: MONTHLY BY REGULATION, not by preference — 'Monthly generator-category determination' is a requirement in its own right, and 'Episodic generation' exists precisely because a generator temporarily crosses a line. Thresholds read from the prose: VSQG at most 100 kg, SQG 100-1,000 kg, LQG 1,000 kg or more.

switches.label: Acute hazardous waste generated per month
switches.question_plain: Do you generate more than 1 kg of acute hazardous waste in a month?
switches.notes: A separate switch from the non-acute quantity because 1 kg of acute waste makes a site an LQG regardless of its non-acute total. Bundling them would hide that.

switches.label: Hazardous waste generator category
switches.question_plain: What is your hazardous waste generator category?
switches.notes: GATES 16 REQUIREMENTS — more than any other switch. COMPUTED from the two kilogram switches rather than asked, which is why it has no depends_on: the dependency model gates on a specific parent VALUE, and this is an arithmetic derivation rather than a gate. jurisdiction_variant = true: Washington's dangerous-waste program is BROADER than federal RCRA, with state-only designations, so the same waste stream can be non-hazardous in Oregon and regulated in Washington (CHEMICAL-OR-WA.md §1.4).

switches.label: PCB equipment or contamination
switches.question_plain: Do you own PCB equipment, store PCB waste, or have legacy equipment of unknown status?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. The trigger explicitly includes 'unknown-status legacy equipment', which is a case where unknown is itself the trigger rather than a gap.

switches.label: Generates or handles used oil
switches.question_plain: Do you generate, store, burn, or market used oil?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Manages universal waste
switches.question_plain: Do you manage batteries, lamps, mercury equipment, pesticides, or aerosol cans as waste?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. jurisdiction_variant: states add their own universal-waste categories.

switches.label: Air permit tier
switches.question_plain: What kind of air permit does this site hold, if any?
switches.notes: Gates the Oregon ACDP, Title V, Title V monitoring and certification, the NSPS/NESHAP screen, and Oregon's greenhouse-gas report. Annual: permits carry annual reporting and fee obligations, and §1.3 flags the ACDP report and fee dates as disputed — verify before stating them.

switches.label: Cleaner Air Oregon applies
switches.question_plain: Has DEQ called this site in under Cleaner Air Oregon, or is a new or modified source triggering a toxics review?
switches.notes: A GENUINE OREGON DISTINCTIVE with no Washington equivalent. Depends on holding an air permit because Cleaner Air Oregon is layered on top of conventional air permitting (§1.3). depends_on_value 'not_none' is a sentinel the loader validates — see the loader's dependency section.

switches.label: Greenhouse gas emissions, tonnes CO2e per year
switches.question_plain: Roughly how many tonnes of CO2 equivalent does this site emit a year?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. TWO THRESHOLDS FROM TWO REGULATORS AND THAT IS THE POINT: Oregon's DEQ report starts at 2,500 tonnes for an air-permitted source; the federal Part 98 report starts at 25,000. A site at 3,000 owes one and not the other, and a single boolean could not say which.

switches.label: Where process wastewater goes
switches.question_plain: Where does your process wastewater go — the sewer, a surface water, the ground, or nowhere?
switches.notes: Gates Oregon's industrial wastewater authorisation and the federal pretreatment standards. 'to_potw' is what brings LOCAL-SEWER into scope — an agency with zero library rows today (TODO 6.5a).

switches.label: Industrial activity exposed to stormwater
switches.question_plain: Is any industrial activity or material exposed to rain, rather than fully sheltered?
switches.notes: Gates Oregon's 1200-Z permit and the federal no-exposure certification — which are opposites: the certification is the route OUT of the permit, so false here is itself a requirement.

switches.label: Aboveground storage tanks present
switches.question_plain: Do you have aboveground storage tanks?
switches.notes: THE INVENTORY FACT, and the parent of oil_storage_aboveground_gallons. Read that switch's note for the cycle this nearly was.

switches.label: Aggregate aboveground oil storage, gallons
switches.question_plain: Roughly how many gallons of oil can you store aboveground in containers of 55 gallons or more?
switches.notes: RENAMED FROM §2.4's oil_storage_1320gal AND MADE NUMERIC, because the threshold belongs in `thresholds` rather than in the identifier. THE CYCLE THIS NEARLY WAS: read in isolation, this depends on knowing the tanks, and the AST inspection requirement's trigger reads 'ASTs subject to SPCC' — which would make aboveground_storage_tanks depend back on this. Both readings are locally correct and together they cycle. DECIDED (DECISIONS.md §37): tanks are the inventory, gallons are computed from it, the arrow goes one way, and the AST requirement's 'subject to SPCC' condition belongs in applies_expression rather than in the switch graph. 42,000 is the buried-container threshold in the same rule.

switches.label: Regulated underground storage tanks
switches.question_plain: Do you have underground storage tanks holding petroleum or another regulated substance?
switches.notes: Gates Oregon UST registration and the detection and operability tests.

switches.label: Offers hazardous materials for transport
switches.question_plain: Do you ship anything that meets a DOT hazard definition?
switches.notes: GATES 13 PHMSA REQUIREMENTS — classification, shipping papers, marking and labelling, placarding, registration, security plan, employee training, cylinder requalification, incident reporting. Company-scoped: offering hazmat is an enterprise activity even when the dock is at one site.

switches.label: Operates its own vehicles
switches.question_plain: Do you run your own trucks, or does a carrier collect everything?
switches.notes: COMPANY-SCOPED. Gates the five FMCSA requirements. The original 2.5L failure invented 'your own vehicles' in its title when the user never said it — DECISIONS.md §4 — so this switch being unknown must produce an ask or a conditional, never an assumption. Per-vehicle facts belong to the equipment layer, not here.

switches.label: Employs CDL drivers
switches.question_plain: Do you employ drivers with a commercial driver's licence?
switches.notes: COMPANY-SCOPED. Gates drug and alcohol testing with Clearinghouse queries, and the hazmat endorsement and TSA assessment.

switches.label: Uses DOT cargo tanks or rail
switches.question_plain: Do you own, lease, load, or unload DOT cargo tanks?
switches.notes: Gates cargo tank inspection and testing, and loading/unloading controls. The 'or rail' half of §2.4's name has NO requirement behind it — no trigger in the library mentions rail.

switches.label: Forklifts or other powered industrial trucks
switches.question_plain: Do you use forklifts or other powered industrial trucks?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4 — the first of TEN equipment switches. The library has 23 requirements with entity_type = 'equipment' and §2.4 proposed no switch for any of them. Gates operator training and pre-use inspection.

switches.label: Overhead or gantry cranes
switches.question_plain: Do you operate overhead or gantry cranes?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Slings used for lifting
switches.question_plain: Do you use slings for lifting?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Portable ladders in use
switches.question_plain: Do employees use portable ladders?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Personal fall-arrest systems in use
switches.question_plain: Do employees use personal fall-arrest systems?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Sprinkler or fixed extinguishing system
switches.question_plain: Does this site have a sprinkler or other fixed extinguishing system?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Portable fire extinguishers provided
switches.question_plain: Are portable fire extinguishers provided at this site?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Employees may use extinguishers
switches.question_plain: Are employees expected to evacuate, or may they fight a small fire?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. A policy rather than an asset, and it changes the training obligation entirely — evacuation-only removes it.

switches.label: Employee alarm system
switches.question_plain: Does this site have an employee alarm system?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Emergency-use or escape respirators
switches.question_plain: Do you keep emergency-use or escape respirators?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4.

switches.label: Piping carrying hazardous substances
switches.question_plain: Do you have piping systems carrying hazardous substances?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Produced by the pipe-labelling determination.

switches.label: Boilers or pressure vessels
switches.question_plain: Do you own or operate a boiler, pressure vessel, or pressure system?
switches.notes: Gates all three Oregon Building Codes Division rows — registration, operating certificate, periodic inspection. A state division, not a local building department.

switches.label: Refrigerant appliances, 50 lb charge or more
switches.question_plain: Do you own or service refrigeration equipment with a charge of 50 lb or more?
switches.notes: The 50 lb charge triggers the leak-repair duties specifically; ownership alone triggers the management rules.

switches.label: Servicing exposes workers to stored energy
switches.question_plain: Does anyone service equipment where unexpected start-up or stored energy could injure them?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. Gates the Lockout/Tagout energy-control programme.

switches.label: Permit-required confined spaces
switches.question_plain: Do employees enter tanks, vessels, pits, or other confined spaces?

switches.label: Respirators required or used
switches.question_plain: Does anyone wear a respirator, required or voluntary?
switches.notes: Voluntary filtering-facepiece use alone is excepted — the trigger says so, and getting that wrong creates a written programme nobody owes.

switches.label: Noise at or above 85 dBA TWA
switches.question_plain: Is anyone exposed to noise at or above 85 dBA over eight hours?
switches.notes: Annual: it is established by monitoring, and monitoring goes stale when a process changes. Boolean rather than numeric because the library names one number and the fact the requirement turns on is 'at or above it'.

switches.label: Reasonably anticipated blood or OPIM exposure
switches.question_plain: Do you have designated first-aid responders, or anyone who could contact blood at work?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4. The trigger explicitly includes designated first-aid responders, which is how a chemical plant with no medical function acquires this obligation.

switches.label: Clinic or hospital in near proximity
switches.question_plain: Is there a clinic or hospital in near proximity to this site?
switches.notes: NOT IN §2.4, and it INVERTS: the requirement fires when this is FALSE. A site with no nearby clinic must have trained first-aid responders on site.

switches.label: Laboratory-scale chemical use
switches.question_plain: Do you have a laboratory using chemicals at laboratory scale?
switches.notes: Gates the Chemical Hygiene Plan, which is a different obligation from HazCom and is often missed because the site already has a HazCom programme.

switches.label: Emergency response posture
switches.question_plain: If there were a significant chemical release, would your people evacuate or respond?
switches.notes: Gates HAZWOPER emergency-response training and medical surveillance. Three values rather than a boolean because 'incidental releases only' is the middle case the standard turns on and it is the most common real answer.

switches.label: Work area reaches a heat index of 80°F
switches.question_plain: Does any work area reach a heat index of 80°F?
switches.notes: SPLIT FROM §2.4's outdoor_work, AND THE NAME MATTERED. §2.4 justified one switch as covering 'heat and wildfire smoke rules'. Oregon's heat rule triggers on 'work area heat index reaches 80°F' — INDOOR AREAS INCLUDED. The name outdoor_work encoded an assumption the rule does not make, and a foundry with no outdoor work would have been told the rule did not apply. jurisdiction_variant: Washington's trigger differs.

switches.label: Exposure may reach PM2.5 of 35.5 µg/m³
switches.question_plain: Could employees be exposed to wildfire smoke at an AQI where PM2.5 reaches 35.5 µg/m³?
switches.notes: The other half of the outdoor_work split. A separate rule with a separate trigger and separate controls; Washington's AQI triggers differ from Oregon's.

switches.label: Flammable liquid quantity against fire-code MAQ
switches.question_plain: Do your flammable liquid quantities exceed the fire code's maximum allowable quantity per control area?
switches.notes: Gates the fire-code hazardous-material permit. 'unknown_maq' is an explicit allowed value rather than an absent row, because MAQ depends on control areas and construction type and is genuinely often unknown — CLAUDE.md §3.2, unknown must stay unknown.

switches.label: Hot work or welding
switches.question_plain: Do you carry out welding, cutting, or other hot work?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — no requirement's trigger names it. §1.3 names hot work as a local fire permit type, and LOCAL-FIRE holds 3 library rows against a much larger real scope (TODO 6.5a). This is that coverage gap arriving from a second direction. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: Spray finishing operations
switches.question_plain: Do you carry out spray finishing or spray application of coatings?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — same LOCAL-FIRE coverage gap as hot_work_welding. §1.3 names it as a fire permit type. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: High-piled combustible storage
switches.question_plain: Do you have high-piled combustible storage?
switches.notes: SEEDED BUT UNUSED — same LOCAL-FIRE coverage gap. §1.3 names it as a fire permit type. DO NOT REMOVE AS DEAD WEIGHT.

switches.label: Regulated explosive materials
switches.question_plain: Do you manufacture, deal in, acquire, or use regulated explosive materials?

switches.label: DEA List I or List II chemicals
switches.question_plain: Do you handle any DEA List I or List II chemicals?

switches.label: Produces pesticide products
switches.question_plain: Do you produce, formulate, repackage, or relabel anything with a pesticidal claim?
switches.notes: Gates EPA product registration and establishment registration, and brings ODA into scope at state level — an agency with zero library rows today.

switches.label: Food-contact or food-grade products
switches.question_plain: Do you make, process, pack, or hold anything that is food or food-contact?

switches.label: Consumer-packaged hazardous products
switches.question_plain: Do you package any hazardous product for household or consumer use?

switches.label: Lead exposure at or above the action level
switches.question_plain: Could anyone be exposed to inorganic lead at or above 30 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA?
switches.notes: Action level 30 µg/m³ TWA. ANNUAL, not static — see the exposure note in DECISIONS.md §38: a lead result from four years ago is not evidence of today's exposure, and the standard mandates periodic monitoring.

switches.label: Benzene exposure at or above the action level
switches.question_plain: Could anyone reach 0.5 ppm benzene as an action level, or 1 ppm as a PEL?
switches.notes: Action level 0.5 ppm, PEL 1 ppm; emergency and dermal criteria also trigger.

switches.label: Respirable crystalline silica at or above the action level
switches.question_plain: Could powders, fillers, maintenance, cutting, or cleanup reach 25 µg/m³ of respirable silica?
switches.notes: Action level 25 µg/m³. ONE SWITCH, FIVE LIBRARY ROWS: the original silica requirement was split into four — exposure assessment, written control plan, medical surveillance, training — and the parent retired. All five share this switch, which is the split working as intended.

switches.label: Hexavalent chromium exposure
switches.question_plain: Is there any chromate, pigment, plating, or welding work that could produce hexavalent chromium?

switches.label: Formaldehyde exposure
switches.question_plain: Is anyone exposed to formaldehyde gas, solution, or a formaldehyde-releasing material?

switches.label: Cadmium exposure
switches.question_plain: Is anyone exposed to cadmium at the action level or doing a covered task?

switches.label: Beryllium exposure
switches.question_plain: Is there beryllium action-level, dermal, symptom, or sensitisation risk?

switches.label: Inorganic arsenic exposure
switches.question_plain: Could anyone reach 5 µg/m³ of inorganic arsenic, or work a covered operation?

switches.label: Asbestos exposure
switches.question_plain: Could anyone disturb or be exposed to asbestos-containing material in older building fabric or equipment?
switches.notes: THE ONE EXPOSURE SWITCH THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON hazardous_chemicals_present. Asbestos comes from the building rather than from the process — a site handling no hazardous chemicals at all can still have ACM in its roof or pipe lagging.

switches.label: 1,3-Butadiene exposure
switches.question_plain: Is anyone occupationally exposed to 1,3-butadiene?

switches.label: Acrylonitrile exposure
switches.question_plain: Is anyone occupationally exposed to acrylonitrile?

switches.label: Ethylene oxide exposure
switches.question_plain: Is there ethylene oxide exposure from reaction, sterilisation, sampling, cylinders, or leaks?

switches.label: Methylene chloride exposure
switches.question_plain: Is anyone occupationally exposed to methylene chloride?
switches.notes: Distinct from tsca_regulated_substances, which gates the EPA risk-management rule for the same chemical. Two regulators, two facts: OSHA cares about worker exposure, EPA about manufacture and use.

switches.label: Vinyl chloride exposure
switches.question_plain: Do you manufacture, react with, or repackage vinyl chloride, or is anyone otherwise exposed?
